claims.text: Counting its overseas departments and territories, France uses 12 standard time zones — more than any other country (Russia and the USA have 11 each when territories are counted).
vo: which country has the most time zones
twelve time zones, thanks to territories scattered across the oceans

claims.text: Russia has 11 time zones, UTC+2 to UTC+12, in one contiguous landmass.
vo: russia stretches across eleven, but all in one block

claims.text: France's zones span UTC−10 (Tahiti / Society Islands) to UTC+12 (Wallis and Futuna); the full set: −10, −9:30, −9, −8, −4, −3, +1, +3, +4, +5, +11, +12.
vo: france runs from tahiti at minus ten to wallis and futuna at plus twelve

claims.text: Arithmetic on the table: Paris (UTC+1 standard time) is 11 hours ahead of Tahiti (UTC−10), so 07:00 in Paris is 20:00 the previous day in Tahiti.
vo: when paris wakes at seven, tahiti is still on yesterday evening

claims.text: Border policy plate (the Europe reveal shows Gibraltar's boundary): Gibraltar is a British overseas territory administered by the United Kingdom and claimed by Spain. No sovereignty asserted.

myths.myth: Russia has the most time zones.
myths.reality: Russia has the most on a single landmass (11); France has 12 once its overseas territories are counted.
